premises: Dislocation nucleation and motion are the primary mechanisms of time-dependent plastic deformation in these coatings at 0.3-0.4 Tm.
Reducing layer thickness to the nanoscale (e.g., 5 nm) imposes geometric confinement that physically restricts dislocation propagation.
This geometric confinement directly limits dislocation interactions and plastic flow, thereby reducing creep strain.
Thicker layers (e.g., 50 nm) provide less geometric constraint, allowing greater dislocation mobility and higher creep rates.
